headline: Founder, VlaDDoS Network | B2B payment partnerships & commercial introductions | Asia · LATAM · Africa
about: I build specific B2B relationships between international merchants, PSPs and aggregators, local payment operators, exchange/OTC businesses, introducers and strategic partners. VlaDDoS Network is an independent partner sourcing and deal origination practice focused on Asia, Latin America and Africa. The starting point is a concrete brief: country, business category, payment flow, operating responsibility and commercial goal. When there is a credible fit, we qualify the scope, obtain permission to introduce and agree the commercial terms in writing. Sourcing mandates, success fees and recurring revenue shares are negotiated individually. VlaDDoS does not hold client funds or execute payments. If you have a specific need or evidenced capability, start at vladdos.com with I NEED or I OFFER.

posts.title: A country flag is not a payment capability
posts.body: A useful local payment conversation needs more than a country name. Which legal entity delivers the service? Which business categories can it onboard? Who handles settlement and reconciliation? Which methods are available for this particular merchant? These are the questions I want a partnership brief to answer. VlaDDoS Network connects a specific need with a relevant business, with scope and permission reviewed before an introduction. Working on a defined country and payment flow? Share that brief through I NEED at vladdos.com.

posts.title: What makes a B2B referral payable?
posts.body: An introduction is a starting point. A payable referral needs a named payer, accepted attribution, an agreed trigger, an eligible fee base, a reporting term and collection evidence. Parent and sub-partner shares also need to be explicit: both affect the economics of the same deal. At VlaDDoS Network, a referral code records a source; a written commercial agreement establishes the earning rules. If you originate relevant merchant or infrastructure relationships, use I OFFER at vladdos.com to discuss the fit before sharing third-party contacts.

posts.title: The partner brief I would bring to a first call
posts.body: One country. One business category. The intended payment flow. A clear description of who is authorised to do what. The capability that is missing. And the commercial outcome that would make the relationship worthwhile. This makes a first conversation more useful than a long company presentation. Merchants, PSPs, local operators and strategic partners can all use the same structure while asking for different outcomes. I am building VlaDDoS Network around that practical brief. Start with I NEED or I OFFER at vladdos.com.

posts.title: Gross fees and founder earnings are different numbers
posts.body: A statement records a fee. A receipt records collection. An affiliate agreement creates an obligation. Those events belong in different parts of the commercial picture. For a small B2B introduction business, retained cash may still include money owed to introducers. Recurring revenue also needs a reporting period and a contractual end date. This is why VlaDDoS Network tracks qualification, introductions, agreements, activation, fees and collection separately. The goal is a repeatable commercial relationship with evidence at each step.

discovery: Which legal entities and decision-makers would sign the agreement?
What country, business category and flow need support now?
What evidence supports each party’s operating role and category eligibility?
Does a prior direct relationship or another referral claim exist?
Who pays VlaDDoS, on what fee base, at which evidenced milestone?
How are refunds, taxes, reporting, collection and recurring termination handled?
What may be shared, with whom, and under whose permission?
cadence: Review inbound enquiries every working day. Research a small number of companies around one concrete demand brief. Send only relevant, manually approved messages through permitted channels. Schedule one useful follow-up after seven days; stop on refusal or opt-out. Review statements and unpaid fees weekly. Judge progress by qualified demand, signed terms, activation and collected net contribution.
